BACKPORT: FROMGIT: LSM: generalize flag passing to security_capable This patch provides a general mechanism for passing flags to the security_capable LSM hook. It replaces the specific 'audit' flag that is used to tell security_capable whether it should log an audit message for the given capability check. The reason for generalizing this flag passing is so we can add an additional flag that signifies whether security_capable is being called by a setid syscall (which is needed by the proposed SafeSetID LSM). Reason for BACKPORT label: aa_capable() function in security/apparmor/capability.c had slightly different logical operator in 4.14. vs latest upstream code. There is no logical difference between the two. Also, change code in security/chromiumos/lsm.c to take advantage of opts arg in security_capable. This allows to refrain from checking the current syscall number when seeing if security_capable is being called from a setid syscall in the chromiumos LSM. vm_tools: maitred: max stateful fs size at boot As a first step toward more dynamic stateful disk sizing, add a btrfs online resize operation to maximize the filesystem within its block device. This will take place on each boot, but it should have minimal overhead if the block device size has not changed (less than 10 ms) and should not take a significant amount of time even when actually resizing, since this will always be expanding into new free space, which doesn't require any shuffling of existing data (growing a 1 GB FS to 2 GB takes less than 100 ms on my test system). Note that this will only work for expanding the disk image; it is not safe to shrink the disk image unless the filesystem is shrunk first, which will never happen in this code path due to the use of 'max' as the size specifier. The approach taken here is enough to allow the virtual block device image to be resized to let the VM consume newly-available free space that wasn't available at VM creation time. Shrinking the VM disk image would need to issue a BTRFS resize operation with an absolute size specified, followed by shrinking the disk image file to that size. However, since we use a sparse backing file for the stateful disk image, free space should already be reclaimed from the VM even if the logical disk size is larger than the available space. Tested by manually expanding the stateful disk image with truncate(1) and restarting the VM, observing the change in filesystem size. FROMLIST: [v3] driver: platform: Support parsing GpioInt 0 in platform_get_irq() ACPI 5 added support for GpioInt resources as a way to provide information about interrupts mediated via a GPIO controller. Several device buses (e.g. SPI, I2C) have support for retrieving an IRQ specified via this type of resource, and providing it directly to the driver as an IRQ number. This is not currently done for the platform drivers, as platform_get_irq() does not try to parse GpioInt() resources. This requires drivers to either have to support only one possible IRQ resource, or to have code in place to try both as a failsafe. While there is a possibility of ambiguity for devices that exposes multiple IRQs, it is easy and feasible to support the common case of devices that only expose one IRQ which would be of either type depending on the underlying system's architecture. This commit adds support for parsing a GpioInt resource in order to fulfill a request for the index 0 IRQ for a platform device. from: https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10824703/ BUG=b:123750725 TEST=boot Kasumi360, observe GPIO work Change-Id: Ibbc9d78546c8189b08d30fd501747ee19bb180f0 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1483850 Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Raul E Rangel <rrangel@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Fix Bluetooth controller event mask config during system suspend As part of CL:1383763, a few Bluetooth controller events were disabled on suspension, to prevent the system from waking up spuriously. This change is applying the same event mask change as in CL:1383763, but instead of overriding the entire set of events mask it selectively masks out or restores the required events during suspend and resume. In addition, the new Set Event Mask operation introduced in this change is using the BlueZ/NewBlue new suspend and resume infrastucture. As part of suspend/resume operations, BlueZ sends a new MGMT command to the kernel to mask out/restore BT specified events. The kernel adds new functions to handle the Set Event Mask request. The request contains a value and mask parameters to enable overriding only selected events. For more details on the Bluetooth/NewBlue suspend infra refer to CL:1454328 BUG=chromium:930973 TEST=suspend and resume of system and verify event mask is set properly by the kernel. npcx: pwm: Turn off pwm signal by setting DCRn greater than CTRn. In npcx pwm modules, there're two ways to turn off pwm signal. One is clearing PWR bit in PWMCTL. The other is setting DCRn's value greater than CTRn's. The current pwm driver adopts the first method. But we saw pwm signal doesn't be turned off by the following sequence: 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); Please notice setting zero in DCRn doesn't mean duty cycle is zero. (NPCX duty cycle: ( (DCRn+1) / (CTRn+1) ) x 100). Hence in step 2, we can observe a very low duty cycle once the driver enabled pwm module. This CL adopts the second method to turn off pwm module. In order to make sure DCRn can be greater than CTRn, we also defined the PWN maximum duty cycle is (0xFFFF -1) since both DCR and CTR are 16-bits registers. BRANCH=none BUG=b:123552920 TEST=No build errors for npcx5/7 series. Test pwm console command on npcx5/7 evbs by the following sequence. 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); And no symptoms are observed.
